title: Dimension-free weak (1,1) bound for the ball maximal function
credit: Question going back to Stein (1980s) and Stein–Strömberg 1983; stated open in Bourgain–Mirek–Stein–Wróbel survey arXiv:1812.00153.
premise_risks: Spector–Stockdale O(sqrt(d) log d) bound (arXiv:2609.05377) is an unrefereed 2026 preprint; the problem statement does not depend on it
Lower-bound literature for balls was checked only through the survey (search budget exhausted)
plain: For a function f on d-dimensional space, the centred maximal function Mf(x) is the largest average of |f| over balls centred at x. A classical theorem says the set where Mf exceeds lambda has volume at most C_d ||f||_1 / lambda. Does one constant C work in every dimension d, or must the best C_d go to infinity?
math: For $d\ge1$ and $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ let $Mf(x)=\sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|^{-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f|$, with $B(x,r)$ the Euclidean ball. Let $C_d$ be the least constant such that $|\{x: Mf(x)>\lambda\}|\le C_d\,\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^d)}$ for all $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ and $\lambda>0$. Decide whether $\sup_{d\ge1}C_d<\infty$.
